top.title: It’s a bit alarming that Radu Drǎgușin is undroppable
top.description: Not the posture you want your best defender to regularly display. | Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images If you’re a calcio doctor unlucky enough to see your door darkened by a Fiorentina side looking for a diagnosis, you’re in for a long day. I can sum it up by saying that literally everything in the team is broken and shows little evidence of knitting together for more than a week or two at a time. It’s hard to pick a primary symptom in such a shambolic club but it’s time for Paolo Vanoli to consider hooking Radu Drǎgușin. The Romania international was one of the summer’s biggest signings. He followed Fabio Paratici from Tottenham Hotspur to Florence. The deal is structured as a loan that becomes an obligation if he starts an unknown number of games; Spurs would get €25 million plus 10% of any future fee. When he arrived, Dustin George-Miller (my counterpart at Cartilage Free Captain) described it as “our old co-Sporting Director doing us a solid” and that probably should have set some alarm bells ringing. Drǎgușin went straight into the XI under Fabio Grosso and stayed there when Vanoli took over. He was shockingly bad in his first appearances and hasn’t improved much since. His lack of pace and trouble scanning down the line were already well-known and his technical limitations weren’t a secret but he’s also struggled in the areas in which he was supposed to excel. Specifically, he’s lost forwards in the box way too easily. That’s a bad quality in a guy who’s cast as a penalty box defender. It can be difficult to judge defenders because they’re usually most noticeable when somebody upstream of them has made a mistake. For example, Drǎgușin getting cooked in space isn’t great but only happens because a midfielder lost a runner and put him in that situation. The revolving door of defensive partners—Luca Ranieri, Marin Pongračić, Viery—has prevented him from building the relationship that any defensive pairing requires. We also have to account for the Fiorentina Bozo Curse, which infects every defender at the club regardless of profile or status. Allowing for mitigation, though, he just doesn’t look up for it. His struggles with Romania make me think it’s not just a Viola problem. Missing nearly two years with injury has obviously set him well back and his agent Florin Manea spoke over the break about the need for patience, predicting that Drǎgușin wouldn’t hit his stride until February. That’s Manea’s job, of course. He sees his client having a tough time and has tried to ease expectations, also citing the faith Paratici has in a player he’s bought twice before. While the sporting director has faith in Drǎgușin, the question is how much the coach should trust him. Drǎgușin is far from the only problem but hasn’t turned in a mistake-free ninety minutes yet. top.title: ‘Coach killers’ – Cam Skattebo will have Giants teammates feeling different to staff, says Jeff Saturday
top.description: Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo will be the most popular player in the locker room, says Jeff Saturday. But do not expect Giants head coach John Harbaugh to feel the same way. Larger than life personality Cam Skattebo has been a lightning rod for discussion all season, and he encapsulated that in Week 11. After promising never to do his backflip celebration again – due to an innocuous injury to Lions star Aidan Hutchinson while celebrating – Skattebo performed an immediate U-turn on the field after the Giants beat the Jaguars. Speaking to Get Up, analyst and former stand-in Colts head coach Jeff Saturday suggested that the Giants coaching staff will not enjoy working with Skattebo. On the other hand, he believes the Giants players will ‘love’ having Skattebo in the trenches with them. When asked if he would love Skattebo as a teammate, Saturday said: “Coaches don’t love them; players love them. Players love them, coaches hate them, they’re coach killers, so I get it. “But you love a dude like that because he’s going to put his head down and run through a wall for you. “Think about how he finished that drive the other night. I understand he fumbled on the drive before, but it’s that type of guy, they’re great locker room guys. “Listen, this season is long, it’s hard, and you need some relief.” Steve Smith Jr agrees Former NFL wide receiver Steve Smith Jr was in agreement that Cam Skattebo would be a popular locker room guy. He explained: “What Skattebo is, is what you call a tone setter. “Whether you’re down or you’re up, you look to your right or your left, and what do you have? You have a Skattebo.” For all the talk about his personality, Skattebo has been the Giants’ most productive running back this season, with 664 scrimmage yards. But the real frustration has been holding the ball. He has five fumbles this season, and this is what John Harbaugh will be desperate to cut out. top.title: Arteta says Arsenal need more luck to kill off games
top.description: Viktor Gyokeres has scored three goals in all competitions this season for Arsenal. [Getty Images] It might be emerging more as a theme than as a major problem, but in recent weeks Arsenal cannot seem to finish off matches when they are on top. In their past nine outings across all competitions, just once have the Gunners won a game by more than a single goal. The latest frustration came in Tuesday's 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund, though perspective is needed. Arsenal might consider it as two points dropped having gone into half-time ahead, but they remain unbeaten in the current Champions League league phase and have not lost at this stage of the competition for more than two years. But of late, despite dominating large parts of matches, Arsenal have had periods where they have dropped off and allowed opponents back into the game. Against Slavia Prague away in the Champions League, after scoring twice in the first half, Arsenal's standards dropped. The same happened against Newcastle in the Premier League last weekend where they found themselves 2-1 behind in the second half having led at the break, before recovering to eventually draw 2-2. They are producing periods of high-level football, but the struggles to consistently turn that into more goals can lead to nervy finishes. In the draw with Bundesliga leaders Dortmund, Arsenal had 30 shots but just four of those attempts were on target. Boss Mikel Arteta mentioned the failure to capitalise post match, though was keen to praise his side's "brilliant performance". "The way we played, bearing in mind the opposition that we played today and what we've done out there, is just something to be very, very pleased [about] because there is very little more that you can demand from the team," Arteta said. "But obviously, the feeling is that we should reward ourselves much more when you put that kind of performance in the amount of chances (and) situations. "There is an element of luck; there is an element of us finishing the actions better. We need to insist because I think what the team has done and shown today, I think it's the right direction." Arsenal held by Borussia Dortmund in Champions League Missing chances or need more luck? Arteta made six changes to the side that drew with Newcastle, with one of the biggest calls to rest striker Kai Havertz and bring in Viktor Gyokeres. The striker has had a difficult season so far, with four of his seven starts coming in the Champions League against opposition where Arsenal have been favourites. However, Gyokeres scored a powerful effort from outside the area to give Arsenal the lead against Dortmund. Overall though, it ended up being a mixed night for the 28-year-old as he missed a header from inside the six-yard-box that would have surely won the game for the Gunners late on. top.title: Injured Giants starter needs surgery: Here’s how much time he’ll miss (UPDATE)
top.description: UPDATE: The Giants on Tuesday placed Greg Newsome on injured reserve, meaning he must miss at least four games. The soonest he can return is Dec. 28 at the Lions. He will miss important matchups with the Colts, 49ers, Seahawks and Browns. *** Giants cornerback Greg Newsome — who had been thriving — might miss the rest of the regular season. Newsome needs surgery to fix his high right ankle sprain and will be sidelined for four to six weeks, according to NFL reporter Jordan Schultz. Newsome got hurt in Sunday’s huge win over the Jaguars. A four-week recovery window might let him return for the Dec. 28 game at the Lions, after he misses matchups with the Colts, 49ers, Seahawks and Browns. A six-week window could let Newsome return for the regular season finale against the Eagles. After visiting the Lions, the Giants travel to Dallas in Week 17. Of course, the Giants might just win the NFC East — they’re currently in the driver’s seat — and make the playoffs for the first time since 2022. The first weekend of the playoffs is Jan. 16-18. It’s possible — but not guaranteed — that Newsome could come back for that game, presuming the Giants win the division. Newsome and fellow starting outside corner Deonte Banks have both excelled this season. So Newsome’s injury is a big blow to the Giants’ surprisingly successful secondary. On Monday, coach John Harbaugh said Newsome would miss multiple weeks — at the minimum. Harbaugh did not rule out surgery for Newsome. top.description: Niko Kovač ‘happy’ with Borussia Dortmund’s mentality against Arsenal Niko Kovač has instilled somewhat of a winning mentality into his Borussia Dortmund side this season. With three 1-0 wins in the Bundesliga, his BVB team faced arguably their biggest challenge of the season on Tuesday night when they faced off against Premier League champions and last season’s UEFA Champions League finalists: Arsenal. Although going behind to a superb Viktor Gyökeres wondergoal in the tenth minute, Maximilian Beier equalised for the Bundesliga leaders ten minutes into the second period, before Jobe Bellingham saw his strike ruled out for an offside. Evidently happy with a 1-1 draw in London , Kovač praised his team’s performance. “It’s a big point for us,” Dortmund’s head coach send in his post-match press conference, attended by Get German Football News . “A big moment for all of us, for the team and for the fans who turned out in such large numbers today. “In the end, we’re happy to take the point.” Although Arsenal registered 28 shots, only four were on target. With a pragmatic approach and steely defence, Dortmund are proving difficult to break down. “We’re here in London, so naturally you have to whether the storm. “I think the team showed a really good side of themselves today. The NFL’s career numbers give the Giants a good reason not to play him like a quarterback who can only hand off: 499 rushing yards and six rushing touchdowns in 11 games that season. top.title: Brandon Aiyuk clears waivers, to visit Commanders on Wednesday
top.description: Former San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk cleared waivers on Tuesday morning after being waived by the team this weekend, and it looks like he’s already got his eyes on his next destination. Aiyuk is now scheduled to visit with the Washington Commanders this Wednesday, per ESPN’s Adam Schefter, as he looks to find a new home soon. The Commanders have long been the destination linked to Aiyuk the most, given his relationship with quarterback Jayden Daniels stemming from their time at Arizona State. There is a clear void there for him to fill, as the Commanders, who beat the Cincinnati Bengals on Monday night to improve to 4-5-1, will be without star receiver Terry McLaurin for the rest of the season. If all pans out, Aiyuk could potentially be the team’s ‘X’ wide receiver opposite Antonio Williams, with Stefon Diggs in the slot. However, the Commanders aren’t the only team interested in Aiyuk, according to Schefter, who tweeted that the wide receiver “is expected to draw interest from a few teams, including the Washington Commanders, and would like to sign soon.” Aiyuk has bought a home in the Washington area, so the Commanders obviously seem like the clearest fit. Other potential teams that could logically make sense also include the Pittsburgh Steelers or even the Seattle Seahawks. The 49ers saga with Aiyuk is now officially over, and it looks like he’s going to play this season on another team.

top.title: Friendship with Julio Rodríguez eases Maikel Garcia’s transition to Mariners
top.description: HOUSTON, TX - MAY 14: Kansas City Royals third baseman Maikel Garcia (11) gets high fives from teammates after hitting a home run in the top of the second inning during the MLB game between the Kansas City Royals and Houston Astros at Daikin Park on May 14, 2025 in Houston, Texas. In fact, Garcia said he was so shocked when the call came through from his agent with news about the trade that he actually hung up on him in his surprise. Thankfully, his next call was easier to take. “I was sitting down outside my house, and I was thinking about it – the trade and everything – in my house in Kansas City, and I see my phone receiving a call from Julio,” said Garcia in a Zoom call with Seattle media on Tuesday. “And he just said, ‘ Villano ’ – Villano is my nickname, it means ”the villain” – so he just said, ‘ Villano , what’s going on?’ And I said to him, ‘you knew, and you didn’t tell me anything!’ He said ‘no, bro. I didn’t know anything, but I’m happy that we have you here, and I know the player that you are, and I’m excited to play together. I know the energy that you have, the passion, and that’s going to help me too.’ Because we have the same passion, the same energy, the same – you know, we love to show emotion in the game, and that’s gonna help the team.” “He gave me a lot of confidence.” Garcia is a passionate player, as anyone who watched him on Team Venezuela in this year’s WBC can attest. top.title: Colts add to QB room after cutting Daniel Jones
top.description: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports Colts add to QB room after cutting Daniel Jones appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Indianapolis Colts have added another quarterback to their roster, signing Shane Buechele off the Buffalo Bills’ practice squad on Tuesday. Indianapolis was left with Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard as its only quarterbacks after waiving Daniel Jones last Friday. Head coach Shane Steichen indicated on Monday that the organization intended to bring in another quarterback to address the situation. Buechele’s arrival gives the Colts three quarterbacks again ahead of Sunday’s matchup against the New York Giants. Richardson has been named the starting quarterback moving forward, while Leonard and Buechele will provide additional depth. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Buechele, 28, entered the NFL in 2021 as an undrafted player after his college career at Texas and SMU. He has spent time with both the Kansas City Chiefs and Bills but has appeared in just one regular-season NFL game. That appearance came with the Chiefs during the 2025 campaign versus the Las Vegas Raiders on January 4. He completed seven of 14 passes for 88 yards and added four rushing yards on one carry in a 14-12 defeat. Buechele’s signing was part of several roster adjustments made by Indianapolis on Tuesday. The Colts promoted defensive end Carl Lawson from the practice squad to the 53-man roster and placed rookie defensive end Caden Curry on injured reserve. They also waived veteran offensive tackle Charlie Heck. Additionally, Indianapolis signed veteran offensive tackle Wanya Morris off the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad and brought tight end Sean McKeon and defensive end Cam Sample onto its practice squad. The Colts, who currently hold a 3-8 record, will now prepare for the Giants with Richardson leading the quarterback room and Buechele providing another option. top.description: Peter Casey-Imagn Images NFL Fantasy Football Week 12 2026 Start ‘Em Sit ‘Em: Kicker appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The best fantasy kicker on any given Sunday isn’t always associated with the highest-scoring offense. For example, Washington showcased this reality on Monday night, when its kicker contributed most of the points in a thrilling victory, while some high-powered teams barely had their kickers attempt a field goal. As we enter Week 12, we can expect more of these contrasts, and the busy holiday schedule means lineup decisions need to be made earlier than usual. Instead of chasing after last week’s top scorer, fantasy managers should assess whether an offense can consistently reach scoring opportunities. top.title: Mark Pope Buyout: How much it would cost if Kentucky were to fire UK Basketball head coach
top.description: Things aren’t necessarily the greatest in and around Kentucky Basketball right now. It’s year three of the Mark Pope era, and the Wildcats are off to a 4-2 start in 2026, with two losses that have been pretty symbolic. The first loss came in a blowout in Chicago against Kansas in the Champions Classic. Kansas is a program that people nationally can compare Kentucky to; the two programs are at the top of the leaderboard for wins in college basketball history, with Kentucky currently holding a four-game lead. The other layer to that loss is that the man who was leading the Jayhawks that evening in the Windy City chose them over Kentucky. Tyran Stokes, a Louisville native, was down to Kentucky and Kansas before ultimately landing in Lawrence for his presumed one year of college basketball. Following the game, we saw a very telling picture of Pope and Stokes shaking hands, along with some words that circulated on social media. The next loss came to Indiana, at Lucas Oil Stadium last Friday night. An Indiana program that Kentucky fans have pointed fingers at for a long time, making fun of the regression of the Hoosiers basketball program. Many members of Big Blue Nation have used the phrase, “at least we’re not Indiana,” when Kentucky has experienced some low points in recent years. The Hoosier fans still hold on to the Christian Watford shot in 2011, which illustrates how far the mighty have fallen. Now, Kentucky added that loss to its resume. In the two contests, Kentucky allowed 89 points and 90 points, providing zero restriction for the opponent when it comes to scoring the ball. On top of that, Kentucky added a one-point miracle victory against Northern Arizona and a very sloppy win against James Madison. So here we are, with Pope’s first year being a great building block but not incredible, and then a very disappointing year two. This year, he had to prove something, and to this point, he hasn’t. That raises the question: how much would it cost Kentucky to fire the former Wildcat? Well, it ain’t cheap. USA TODAY Network reported that Pope’s contract shows that Kentucky would owe Pope 75% of the $17.25 million left on his contract heading into this season as a buyout. That means the school would owe Pope about $13 million if he’s fired on April 1, 2027. This comes on the heels of Kentucky firing its football coach, Mark Stoops, last December, a move that also came with a hefty price tag. With games against a feisty Wichita State team coming to Rupp Arena this Friday, a road game to Virginia, a home game against Louisville, and a neutral site game in New York against North Carolina, it won’t get much easier anytime soon. Things have been trending downward this season for Kentucky, and if something doesn’t change for the better soon, J Batt may have a decision to make in his first year as the University of Kentucky AD.

He commended the NUC for its efforts in upholding academic standards in Nigeria’s tertiary education system, noting that ESUT had prioritised practical training for staff and students to equip them with the skills needed to address challenges within their immediate environment and the country at large. The Vice-Chancellor disclosed that the university had signed a partnership agreement with a Qatar-based Information and Communication Technology (ICT) firm, Vertex Labs, to establish a Centre of Excellence in Artificial Intelligence (AI). According to him, the initiative builds on the selection of ESUT by the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) as a South-East Centre of Excellence in Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, Cybersecurity and other related fields. Professor Okolie also disclosed that the university management had inaugurated an ICT Innovation Hub to provide staff and students with practical training and professional certification programmes that would enhance their employability and economic independence after graduation. He emphasised the importance of engineering in driving the university’s innovation agenda, adding that the institution makes adequate preparations for accreditation exercises by setting aside special funds ahead of time. The Vice-Chancellor further acknowledged TETFund’s contributions towards the procurement of equipment required for accreditation exercises and assured the visiting teams of the full support and cooperation of the university management. Speaking at the ESUT Council Chamber, the leader of the Civil Engineering accreditation team, Professor Mohammed Saidu, said the exercise was not intended to witch-hunt the university but to objectively assess its compliance with established academic standards. top.title: Jim Harbaugh’s ‘Green Dot’ Answer May Be The Nail In The Coffin For Chargers Tenure
top.description: An anonymous NFL executive has predicted that Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh will retire at the end of the 2026 campaign Getty This season has been brutal for the Los Angeles Chargers for so many reasons. The team is 1-9 on the year and to make matters worse head coach Jim Harbaugh just had a confusing answer in a press conference which makes for a really bad look given the team’s struggles. When asked by reporters which defensive player was wearing the “green dot” meaning which player on defense had a radio receiver in his helmet to receive calls from the sidelines, Harbaugh did not know. “Um, a few, I think, uh — who had the green dot? — I’m not for sure. Marlowe Wax, Del’Shawn. Uh, Troy might have had a green dot as well,” he said before asking a staffer who had the green dot. Maybe if the Chargers were having a decent season and were on track to finish 11-6 for a third straight season his answer wouldn’t be so uniformly criticized. Yet, when the team is so bad and coaching has been a major question mark it is just jarring that the coach doesn’t know something that it seems like he should. Harbaugh is not a defensive coach. He was a quarterback in the NFL so obviously he understands that side of the game more, but he should still know what is going on with the defense. Perhaps the fact that he isn’t a playcaller on either side of the ball is why he is not as clued in to what is going on. Do the Chargers need a different style of coach going forward? This controversy really raises the question of what it is that Harbaugh really does. He has refused to take over playcalling duties from offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel even though his tenure has been a trainwreck . He obviously isn’t super invested in what is going on defensively if he doesn’t know the answer to a fairly simple question, so what value is he providing? Clearly, the Chargers thought that he could come in with his track record of success and bring some of that Harbaugh magic to Southern California. Whatever he was doing worked pretty well the last two seasons but going forward one cannot help but wonder whether his head coaching style is what’s best for the Chargers. Someone who knows all the details and is heavily involved, even if they aren’t necessarily calling plays, is what may be needed to get things turned around. The only problem is that the Chargers probably aren’t in a position to fire him given how much money is left on his contract. Perhaps it simply needs to be made clear to him that he needs to be more involved going forward otherwise his job may be in jeopardy should embarrassing episodes like this continue with the product on the field being as bad as it is. top.title: Chiefs Face Worry Over Kenneth Walker Situation Before Thanksgiving Bills Game

But if Walker were to miss this week’s critical game against the Buffalo Bills, it could signal a more significant concern for the Chiefs down the final stretch of the season, an analyst suggests. Chiefs Running Back Could Have Bigger Problems SI.com’s Joshua Brisco responded to a fan’s question about what the Chiefs might do if Walker is unable to play on Thursday night against the Buffalo Bills. Brisco noted that, while Walker appears to be on track to return, another setback could have long-term implications. “To fully wade into a hypothetical that might be irrelevant by the time Tuesday’s injury report comes out: If Walker doesn’t play in Buffalo, I think you have to have some level of concern about his timeline and expectations for the rest of the year, simply due to the possibility that a short-term injury, downplayed by the team, could be lingering much longer than the player and team expected,” Brisco wrote. “That’s always alarming until the player returns and looks like their pre-injury self.” The Chiefs certainly got some good news on Walker on Tuesday, with the running back returning to practice, but his status for Thursday’s game is far from certain. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid warned that the running back wasn’t expected to do a lot in his return to practice. “We’ll see how he does. top.title: ‘Not good enough’ – Haaland unhappy as Man City’s struggles continue
top.description: Manchester City's Erling Haaland appeals to officials during the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Manchester City and Napoli at the Etihad Stadium. (is associated with: «‘Not good enough’ – Haaland unhappy as Man City’s struggles continue») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Erling Haaland felt Manchester City were “not good enough” after they snatched a 2-2 draw at home to Napoli in the Champions League. Rayan Cherki scored an 86th-minute equalizer as City came from behind for a second time to avoid defeat at the hands of the Italians on Tuesday. The result continued a frustrating run of form for City, who have won just one of their last seven games in all competitions. City striker Haaland told TNT Sports: “We tried to push at the end for a goal but we couldn’t – not good enough and we let them in too easily. “We were not able to control and attack the game in the way we want. “Football is easy and difficult – when you win it’s easy and you know what to do. When you don’t you start questioning everything. “The perfect thing would be to not think but it’s not so easy. “We have so much quality so it’s about getting the quality out in every payer. “We have to regroup, stay positive and bring energy on the pitch and try to do our best.” After a tame first half, City fell behind to a goal from former Manchester United striker Rasmus Hojlund after 55 minutes. Ayyoub Bouaddi pulled them back into the game but City needed to fight back again after Noa Lang restored Napoli’s lead with a fine volley 14 minutes from time. Cherki’s leveller was a fine individual effort but the Frenchman felt the overall performance had been a flat one. He said: “I don’t care about scoring, I just want to win. We played good but we didn’t play with energy, we need to do more. “Today was like the last games, we need to work more.” City manager Enzo Maresca laughed when told of Cherki’s comments, insisting there were positives to build on. The Italian said: “No, I think tonight we pressed very aggressive, we recovered the ball most of the time. Off the ball I think the team was good, from my point of view. “We created a lot of chances but it was difficult. We expected Napoli to play a waiting game in a low block. “We conceded few chances, and the goals we conceded could have been avoided. “There is a degree of regret we didn’t win but when you can’t win, don’t lose. We take the point and go forward.”

nigeria.title: 2027: Shunning ethnicity and religion
nigeria.description: As Nigerians prepare for next year’s general elections, they must move beyond the unhealthy politics of ethnicity and religion in the campaigns and choice of leaders. While diversity and equitable representation deserve recognition, they must not take precedence over competence, accountability and proven track records of service delivery. Nigeria cannot build a united democracy on religious intolerance, ethnic suspicion and political exclusion. The country’s numerous ethnic nationalities, languages, cultures and religious traditions should be sources of strength. Sadly, politicians and influential interest groups increasingly manipulate these identities to deepen divisions, promote intolerance and weaken national unity. The emerging political atmosphere is reminiscent of the 2023 general elections, when ethnic and religious considerations dominated campaigns and public discourse. The European Union Election Observation Mission (EU-EOM), in its final report, expressed concern over divisive language and the mobilisation of ethnic and religious sentiments during the elections. It is particularly disturbing that candidates are increasingly judged not by their competence, records and policy proposals but by their faith, language or geographical origin. Political differences or disagreements are sinisterly framed as grievances against entire ethnic or religious communities. Such tendencies undermine democratic competition and threaten peaceful coexistence. The Constitution (1999, as amended) provides clear safeguards against this divisive politics. Section 10 prohibits the adoption of any religion as a state religion, while Section 15 promotes national integration and prohibits discrimination based on place of origin, religion, ethnic or linguistic association. Section 42 further guarantees protection against discrimination on these grounds. These provisions must translate into political practice. No Nigerian should be denied the opportunity to aspire to public office because of religious belief or ethnic origin. Equally, political appointments and access to public opportunities must be guided by fairness, merit and competence rather than narrow identity considerations. Religious leaders must also recognise their responsibility to promote peace, tolerance and mutual respect. Pulpits and religious platforms should never become instruments for spreading political hatred or hostility against people of other faiths. Traditional rulers, community leaders and ethnic associations must similarly resist manipulation by partisan interests. Cultural pride should never become an excuse for intolerance. nigeria.description: “We cannot demand twenty-first-century compliance with twentieth-century communication .” — Mohammed Idris Bultu The first part of this article examined taxation as a relationship between the state and the citizen and ended with a fundamental question: what does the state owe the citizen after collecting his money? Two thoughtful responses to that article have since helped to sharpen the inquiry considerably. Barrister Muhammad Betara, an Abuja-based lawyer, approached the subject mainly from the standpoint of law and public administration, while Mohammed Idris Bultu, a Tax Controller with the Nigeria Revenue Service in Kano, responded from the practical experience of a tax administrator who encounters taxpayers, assessments, compliance and collection in the field. Taken together, their observations provide an important bridge between theory, law and administrative practice. Barrister Betara’s central point is that Nigeria is not without a legal framework for taxation. On the contrary, the Constitution and the recent tax reforms impose clear duties upon citizens and create elaborate machinery for assessment, collection and administration. According to him, Section 24(f) of the 1999 Constitution places upon every citizen the duty to declare his income honestly and pay his tax promptly. That obligation is direct and enforceable. At the same time, the Constitution declares that the security and welfare of the people shall be the primary purpose of government and places upon the state broad responsibilities relating to economic welfare, justice and social order. Betara’s important observation is that an imbalance exists between these two sides of the constitutional bargain. The citizen’s obligation to pay tax is concrete and enforceable, while many of the wider welfare obligations of government cannot be enforced by the citizen in quite the same manner. This immediately raises the problem of reciprocity. If the state possesses machinery to compel compliance from the citizen, what equivalent machinery exists which enables the citizen to compel transparency, accountability and adequate service delivery from the state? This lies very close to the heart of the distinction between taxation and imposition. The recent tax reforms have sought to strengthen and modernise the administrative capacity of government. They aim to harmonise tax administration, rationalise procedures, improve taxpayer identification, expand the tax base and provide mechanisms for objection and appeal. Barrister Betara therefore makes the important point that the Nigerian problem is not simply the absence of laws. The problem is that the machinery of collection often appears stronger, more visible and more immediate than the machinery of public accountability. Budget revision is not inherently a sign of failure. Governments should adjust spending plans when revenue, financing conditions or obligations change. An unrealistic budget does not become credible merely because it has been signed into law. The more important signal is what remains unchanged: a ₦31.457 trillion fiscal deficit and planned new borrowing of ₦29.218 trillion. Nigeria is reducing expenditure, but it is not reducing the gap between what government earns and what it intends to spend. Capital expenditure is estimated at ₦26.232 trillion, while the deficit remains equivalent to 5.64 per cent of GDP. The borrowing plan comprises ₦18.428 trillion in domestic financing and ₦10.790 trillion from external sources. The government says its proposed $7.7 billion foreign loan will fund an existing external-borrowing provision rather than increase the approved envelope. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Anchorage Digital Sets Up Asset Manager to Offer Bitcoin Yield to Clients Anchorage Digital, the first federally chartered crypto bank in the U.S., is moving into asset management with a new subsidiary that will offer custody clients a way to earn yield on their bitcoin. The unit, called 61st Parallel Asset Management, is expected to start operating by early December, CEO Nathan McCauley said in an interview to CoinDesk. Its first product will be a bitcoin-denominated fund, meaning returns are measured in BTC rather than dollars. The name nods to the city of Anchorage, Alaska, which sits at 61 degrees north latitude. “We have increasingly heard clients say they want to earn on top of the assets they hold at Anchorage — something that’s very common among the large financial institutions of the world,” McCauley said. Anchorage has filed a Form ADV, the disclosure document investment advisers use to register with the Securities and Exchange Commission or state regulators, or to report as exempt advisers. The form covers a firm’s ownership, business, assets under management, fees and conflicts of interest. As of Tuesday afternoon, the SEC’s public adviser database showed no record for 61st Parallel, so the filing’s details were not yet public. Paperwork dating back to summer The entity itself is not new. New York state records show that 61st Parallel Asset Management LLC, a Delaware company, registered to do business in New York on July 8, listing an office on Park Avenue South in Manhattan. Anchorage already lets clients earn on some holdings. Its website lists staking, which pays rewards for helping secure proof-of-stake networks, and a separate rewards product for eligible assets. Bitcoin runs on proof-of-work and cannot be staked natively. Anchorage has not said publicly how the fund will generate yield, what it will charge or which clients will qualify. Those details matter to bitcoin holders, because bitcoin pays no interest on its own. Common ways to earn on it include lending coins out, posting them as collateral or selling options against them, and each carries its own risk. Public companies have already tested some of those approaches. Trump Media disclosed this month that it had pledged about 73% of its bitcoin to an options program in which the counterparty can rehypothecate, or reuse, the coins. entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? entertainment.title: Esther Adeyanju: This International Men’s Day, Let’s Make Room for Men’s Vulnerability
entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? Surely, a man’s worth cannot be reduced to his bank balance, job title or ability to convince everyone that he has everything under control. There must be room for men who are still becoming. I can sum it up by saying that literally everything in the team is broken and shows little evidence of knitting together for more than a week or two at a time. It’s hard to pick a primary symptom in such a shambolic club but it’s time for Paolo Vanoli to consider hooking Radu Drǎgușin. The Romania international was one of the summer’s biggest signings. He followed Fabio Paratici from Tottenham Hotspur to Florence. The deal is structured as a loan that becomes an obligation if he starts an unknown number of games; Spurs would get €25 million plus 10% of any future fee. When he arrived, Dustin George-Miller (my counterpart at Cartilage Free Captain) described it as “our old co-Sporting Director doing us a solid” and that probably should have set some alarm bells ringing. Drǎgușin went straight into the XI under Fabio Grosso and stayed there when Vanoli took over. He was shockingly bad in his first appearances and hasn’t improved much since. His lack of pace and trouble scanning down the line were already well-known and his technical limitations weren’t a secret but he’s also struggled in the areas in which he was supposed to excel. Specifically, he’s lost forwards in the box way too easily. That’s a bad quality in a guy who’s cast as a penalty box defender. It can be difficult to judge defenders because they’re usually most noticeable when somebody upstream of them has made a mistake. For example, Drǎgușin getting cooked in space isn’t great but only happens because a midfielder lost a runner and put him in that situation. sports.title: Brandon Aiyuk clears waivers, to visit Commanders on Wednesday
sports.description: Former San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk cleared waivers on Tuesday morning after being waived by the team this weekend, and it looks like he’s already got his eyes on his next destination. Aiyuk is now scheduled to visit with the Washington Commanders this Wednesday, per ESPN’s Adam Schefter, as he looks to find a new home soon. The Commanders have long been the destination linked to Aiyuk the most, given his relationship with quarterback Jayden Daniels stemming from their time at Arizona State. There is a clear void there for him to fill, as the Commanders, who beat the Cincinnati Bengals on Monday night to improve to 4-5-1, will be without star receiver Terry McLaurin for the rest of the season. If all pans out, Aiyuk could potentially be the team’s ‘X’ wide receiver opposite Antonio Williams, with Stefon Diggs in the slot. However, the Commanders aren’t the only team interested in Aiyuk, according to Schefter, who tweeted that the wide receiver “is expected to draw interest from a few teams, including the Washington Commanders, and would like to sign soon.” Aiyuk has bought a home in the Washington area, so the Commanders obviously seem like the clearest fit. Other potential teams that could logically make sense also include the Pittsburgh Steelers or even the Seattle Seahawks. The 49ers saga with Aiyuk is now officially over, and it looks like he’s going to play this season on another team.

sports.title: Mark Pope Buyout: How much it would cost if Kentucky were to fire UK Basketball head coach
sports.description: Things aren’t necessarily the greatest in and around Kentucky Basketball right now. It’s year three of the Mark Pope era, and the Wildcats are off to a 4-2 start in 2026, with two losses that have been pretty symbolic. The first loss came in a blowout in Chicago against Kansas in the Champions Classic. Kansas is a program that people nationally can compare Kentucky to; the two programs are at the top of the leaderboard for wins in college basketball history, with Kentucky currently holding a four-game lead. The other layer to that loss is that the man who was leading the Jayhawks that evening in the Windy City chose them over Kentucky. Tyran Stokes, a Louisville native, was down to Kentucky and Kansas before ultimately landing in Lawrence for his presumed one year of college basketball. Following the game, we saw a very telling picture of Pope and Stokes shaking hands, along with some words that circulated on social media. The next loss came to Indiana, at Lucas Oil Stadium last Friday night. An Indiana program that Kentucky fans have pointed fingers at for a long time, making fun of the regression of the Hoosiers basketball program. Many members of Big Blue Nation have used the phrase, “at least we’re not Indiana,” when Kentucky has experienced some low points in recent years. The Hoosier fans still hold on to the Christian Watford shot in 2011, which illustrates how far the mighty have fallen. Now, Kentucky added that loss to its resume. In the two contests, Kentucky allowed 89 points and 90 points, providing zero restriction for the opponent when it comes to scoring the ball. On top of that, Kentucky added a one-point miracle victory against Northern Arizona and a very sloppy win against James Madison. So here we are, with Pope’s first year being a great building block but not incredible, and then a very disappointing year two. This year, he had to prove something, and to this point, he hasn’t. That raises the question: how much would it cost Kentucky to fire the former Wildcat? Well, it ain’t cheap. USA TODAY Network reported that Pope’s contract shows that Kentucky would owe Pope 75% of the $17.25 million left on his contract heading into this season as a buyout. That means the school would owe Pope about $13 million if he’s fired on April 1, 2027. This comes on the heels of Kentucky firing its football coach, Mark Stoops, last December, a move that also came with a hefty price tag. With games against a feisty Wichita State team coming to Rupp Arena this Friday, a road game to Virginia, a home game against Louisville, and a neutral site game in New York against North Carolina, it won’t get much easier anytime soon. Things have been trending downward this season for Kentucky, and if something doesn’t change for the better soon, J Batt may have a decision to make in his first year as the University of Kentucky AD.

sports.title: Jim Harbaugh’s ‘Green Dot’ Answer May Be The Nail In The Coffin For Chargers Tenure
sports.description: An anonymous NFL executive has predicted that Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh will retire at the end of the 2026 campaign Getty This season has been brutal for the Los Angeles Chargers for so many reasons. The team is 1-9 on the year and to make matters worse head coach Jim Harbaugh just had a confusing answer in a press conference which makes for a really bad look given the team’s struggles. When asked by reporters which defensive player was wearing the “green dot” meaning which player on defense had a radio receiver in his helmet to receive calls from the sidelines, Harbaugh did not know. “Um, a few, I think, uh — who had the green dot? — I’m not for sure. Marlowe Wax, Del’Shawn. Uh, Troy might have had a green dot as well,” he said before asking a staffer who had the green dot. Maybe if the Chargers were having a decent season and were on track to finish 11-6 for a third straight season his answer wouldn’t be so uniformly criticized. Yet, when the team is so bad and coaching has been a major question mark it is just jarring that the coach doesn’t know something that it seems like he should. Harbaugh is not a defensive coach. He was a quarterback in the NFL so obviously he understands that side of the game more, but he should still know what is going on with the defense. Perhaps the fact that he isn’t a playcaller on either side of the ball is why he is not as clued in to what is going on. Do the Chargers need a different style of coach going forward? This controversy really raises the question of what it is that Harbaugh really does. He has refused to take over playcalling duties from offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel even though his tenure has been a trainwreck . He obviously isn’t super invested in what is going on defensively if he doesn’t know the answer to a fairly simple question, so what value is he providing? Clearly, the Chargers thought that he could come in with his track record of success and bring some of that Harbaugh magic to Southern California. Whatever he was doing worked pretty well the last two seasons but going forward one cannot help but wonder whether his head coaching style is what’s best for the Chargers. Someone who knows all the details and is heavily involved, even if they aren’t necessarily calling plays, is what may be needed to get things turned around. The only problem is that the Chargers probably aren’t in a position to fire him given how much money is left on his contract. Perhaps it simply needs to be made clear to him that he needs to be more involved going forward otherwise his job may be in jeopardy should embarrassing episodes like this continue with the product on the field being as bad as it is. His team is credited with the development of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in the late ’80s during his time at Bell Labs. He later oversaw the development of Meta’s Llama herd of models as chief AI scientist before shifting gears away from LLMs to world model architectures like JEPA. technology.title: 'We are not ShinyHunters,' says criminal hacking crew that looks and acts just like ShinyHunters
technology.description: Inception, a new data theft and extortion gang that security researchers have theorized is a rebrand of the ShinyHunters group, “reject[s] this attribution” and claims it has no affiliation with any prior cybercrime enterprise. In a lengthy statement posted Tuesday and shared on X, the extortionists insist that they are a new group, with new operators, and that their alleged social engineering attacks aren’t copying anyone - but rather just abusing the weakest link in an organization’s security: “a human being holding a phone.” The rant follows a Monday report by Okta Threat Intelligence - along with social media speculation since Inception’s inception last week - that the newly emerged group is very likely ShinyHunters with a different name . Okta’s researchers based their analysis on the two groups’ shared infrastructure, plus Inception’s nearly identical tactics: voice phishing , during which the scammers trick targets into entering credentials into phishing pages and approving multi-factor authentication (MFA) requests. Inception apparently took offense to this. “We would like to address this once, clearly, and only once,” the crims' statement says. “We are not ShinyHunters. We were never ShinyHunters. We are Inception.” The gang argues that its overlapping domain registrars, hosting providers, and DNS services don’t prove anything. These are commodity services, “available to anyone who can pay for them,” Inception wrote. Plus, their similar methodologies don't necessarily make Inception a reboot. “That is not theft of tradecraft,” they wrote. “It is acknowledgment of a good idea – the same way every group after LockBit used a leak site, and nobody called them LockBit.” “Inception is a new group, with new operators, our own objectives, and our own name,” the statement continues. “What we share with the past is plumbing.” To be fair, the new crime crew has every reason to distance itself from ShinyHunters. That gang’s September FBI hack - plus several earlier digital heists during which the criminals stole information belonging to millions of people, including cancer patients , university and K-12 students - put a massive target on its collective backs. And while at least three ShinyHunters suspects were arrested in September and October, there's no confirmation that authorities have dismantled the entire operation. Plus, as a ShinyHunters spokesperson told The Register in an earlier interview, they and others in the crew started off as GnosticPlayers before rebranding as ShinyHunters in 2020 - so a reboot isn’t beyond the realm of possibility. Inception, for its part, says it “will not comment further on the ghost of ShinyHunters,” and it has its own work to do. And by work, it means copying ShinyHunters' playbook, stealing corporate data, and extorting victim companies for massive sums of money.®

science.title: SpaceX launches secretive spy satellites from California for US Space Force (video)
science.description: null SpaceX launched another classified mission for the U.S. Space Force (USSF) today (Nov. 24), sending an unknown payload toward orbit from California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base's Space Launch Complex-4E at TK11:08 a.m. ET (1508 GMT) , carrying the U.S. Space Force's USSF-266 mission. It was the fourth mission SpaceX has launched for the military branch this month. While details about the mission's payload weren't disclosed, it's the fifth space launch in support of U.S. national security in the last two weeks, and comes amid efforts by the Space Force to expand its communications and tracking capabilities. (Image credit: SpaceX) About two and a half minutes after liftoff, Falcon 9's first-stage booster separated from the rocket's upper stage, which continued toward low Earth orbit with the classified payload. The booster, meanwhile, began a descent toward SpaceX's Of Course I Still Love You droneship in the Pacific Ocean, where it touched down approximately eight and a half minutes after launch. Tuesday's launch marked the 29th flight for this Falcon 9 booster, B1081, which previously launched NASA 's Crew-7 astronaut mission to the International Space Station , the PACE and EarthCARE science satellites , two other classified Space Force launches (USSF-153 and USSF-481), and 16 Starlink missions. Previous classified Space Force launches have fueled speculation about the possible deployment of SpaceX's Starshield satellites, which are designed for national security applications. Starshield is an adapted spacecraft design developed from SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation that supports military operations with capabilities like Earth observation and secure communications. SpaceX has not confirmed whether USSF-266 is carrying Starshield spacecraft. USSF-266 follows three other classified Space Force missions launched by SpaceX from Vandenberg earlier this month: USSF-432 on Nov. 6, USSF-627 on Nov. 11 and USSF-317 on Nov. 20, as well as a National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) launch, NROL-136, on Nov. 22. Those missions were also launched aboard Falcon 9 rockets, also with undisclosed payloads.

science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 24, 1947: The US Navy launches the 1st Aerobee sounding rocket, but it didn't reach space
science.description: null On Nov. 24, 1947, the U.S. Navy launched the first Aerobee rocket into the sky, but it never reached space. Aerobee was a suborbital sounding rocket designed to study Earth's atmosphere . After World War 2, the United States started reusing erman V-2 rockets for this kind of research. When they started running out of V-2 rockets , the United States constructed its own rockets that were similar but cheaper to build and to launch. In the weeks leading up to the first Aerobee mission, three test flights were launched. Those tests used a dummy version of Aerobee with a live booster to see if the two stages would separate properly. On Aerobee's first real flight, the rocket flew about 35 miles high. That's below the 62-mile (100 kilometers) upper limit for the boundary of space . (NASA and the U.S. military typically consider 50 miles the edge of space.) Mission control cut the flight short after about 30 seconds, because Aerobee started to yaw, and they wanted to keep it from going completely out of control. The first Aerobee sounding rocket launched on Nov. 24, 1947 under a project led by the U.S. Navy. (Image credit: U.S. Navy) Why it mattered Billed as the " most successful sounding rocket of the space age ," the initial Aerobee rocket was suborbital rocket designed to launch experment payload of up to 100 pounds (45 kilograms) to an altitude of 75 miles (121 kilometers) or so. "The Aerobee was designed to carry instruments aloft to collect data on the upper atmosphere and to place small animals in a weightless condition for physiological studies," the U.S. National Museum of the United States Air Force wrote in a mission overview . "It was launched by a solid-propellant booster engine of 18,000 pounds thrust that burned for only two and a half seconds." An Aerobee suborbital sounding rocket of the type designed to study Earth's atmosphere. (Image credit: NMMSH) While the first Aerobee rocket did not reach space , many more made successful launches in the decades that followed. Engineers made a steady stream of upgrades to the the Aerobee rocket, allowing to fly higher and launch heavier payloads into space. It was an Aerobee rocket that launched two Phillipine monkeys on a mission to study how the effects of rapid launch acceleration might affect their bodies, an experiment that was among the frst human physiology tests that paved the way for human spaceflight . More than 1,000 Aerobee rockets have launched since then, and the last one flew in January of 1985. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

science.title: Teams Lock in Mission Architecture for NASA’s SR-1 Freedom
science.description: 5 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) NASA’s Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom, the first fission-powered spacecraft to travel beyond Earth orbit, cruises past Mars in this artist’s concept, demonstrating nuclear electric propulsion in deep space. Credit: NASA/Jonathan North NASA completed a major review for Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom and locked in key elements of the spacecraft, which is targeted to launch in 2028 and demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion in deep space for the first time. Experts from across the agency, the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), and industry met at NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland for a major SR-1 mission design review in October. Several key decisions were made, propelling the mission from an early concept toward a defined spacecraft design. “SR-1 marks a pivotal step in how we travel through the solar system,” said Steve Sinacore, SR-1 Freedom program director. “This mission will be the first freight run on the railroad of the solar system, and the decisions we’re making now are laying the tracks for every nuclear-powered spacecraft that follows.” Planned for launch in late 2028, SR-1 will use both nuclear and solar power to deliver SkyFall , a capsule carrying three next-generation helicopters, to Mars. Once deployed, the helicopters will study Martian geology and climate history, explore new terrain, and search for signs of subsurface ice. As NASA prepares for more ambitious exploration missions, future spacecraft and surface operations will require significantly more power than current systems can provide, particularly in environments where sunlight is limited or unavailable. SR-1 will demonstrate how fission power can enable long-duration missions, pave the way for reliable surface power systems to support NASA’s future Moon Base , and enable exploration deeper into the solar system. Key design decisions The SR-1 Freedom spacecraft design has evolved since NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman first introduced the concept in March at the agency’s Ignition event, where leadership shared plans to develop a fission-powered spacecraft in time for the next Mars launch window. One significant change is to use a shorter boom than the one shown in early illustrations. The boom separates the reactor from the spacecraft’s main body, known as the Power and Propulsion Element. The shorter boom will reduce weight, simplify assembly, and help streamline the spacecraft’s design. Planned for launch in late 2028, Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom will use both nuclear and solar power to deliver SkyFall to Mars. This infographic explains the components of the spacecraft. Credit: NASA/David Lam NASA and DOE experts also determined that improvements in shielding and spacecraft design will allow the reactor to operate closer to the rest of the spacecraft. This will simplify integration while maintaining the radiation protection needed for spacecraft electronics and the SkyFall payload.

science.title: 1st-ever detection of a dying star's 'final nuclear heartbeat' challenges what we know about our sun's eventual death
science.description: null As ubiquitous as the sun is to us today, our star is not eternal; one day, albeit in billions of years, it will die. While massive stars die in supernova explosions, the sun and stars of similar mass die quieter deaths. But that doesn't mean these stars completely go out with a whimper. New observations collected using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), the world's largest radio telescope comprised of 66 antennas in northern Chile, reveal that the sun's death throes may be different from what scientists had initially believed. NASA Jet Propulsion Lab (JPL) researcher Raghvendra Sahai, who led the investigation, explained the shape the ALMA observations took: "It's essentially a physical snapshot of an event that, until now, we've mostly inferred from theoretical models. We've caught, for the first time, a star's final nuclear heartbeat, frozen in gas." Sun-like stars "die" when they run out of hydrogen in their cores. This means that the fusion of hydrogen to helium ceases in the stellar core, and because this nuclear process is a star's main energy source, the star no longer has the outward push to support itself against the inward push of its own gravity. As the star's core collapses to create a stellar remnant called a white dwarf , the outer layers where hydrogen is still fusing to form helium swell out. This expansion leads to a relatively short-lived " red giant " phase. Eventually, these outer layers will cool and disperse, leaving the central white dwarf surrounded by a so-called "planetary nebula" shell of debris. During the red giant phase, as the stellar core is surrounded by shells of hydrogen and helium, these layers are occasionally rocked by flares in nuclear activity called thermal pulses. During these episodes, stellar material is flung into space. To better understand this phase in stellar evolution, the team focused ALMA on a star called IRAS 06530-0213, located around 12,000 light-years away in the constellation Monoceros. This revealed a giant ring of gas that appears to be a frozen fossil of the star's last thermonuclear flare-up. This thermonuclear fossil rings an hourglass-shaped planetary nebula in the act of forming. "Most of us think of stars as unchanging points of light, but this is a real-time snapshot of a star's death throes," Sahai said. "It's the brief, violent transition between a bloated red giant and a glowing planetary nebula, frozen mid-action." science.title: Double asteroid solar eclipse caught on camera | Space photo of the day for Nov. 24, 2026
science.description: null (Image credit: ESA) A spacecraft far from Earth beamed home a rare sight: a solar eclipse caused by one asteroid casting its shadow on another. What is it? The image shows the Didymos double asteroid system , which consists of the larger Didymos and its moonlet, Dimorphos. In this image, Dimorphos' shadow can be seen on the surface of Didymos. The image was captured by the European Space Agency's (ESA's) Hera probe, which was sent to rendezvous with Didymos. Once there, Hera's job is to inspect the system to study the aftermath of NASA's historic DART mission (Double Asteroid Redirect Test), which slammed a kinetic impactor into Dimorphos in September 2022 in an attempt to alter its orbit and thus the trajectory of the entire two-asteroid system. Such missions, should they ever be needed in the future, could potentially redirect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. Why is it incredible? For one, this image is incredible given that it was beamed home by Hera while it approaches Didymos some 121 million miles (195 million kilometers) away from Earth. But more than that, this image reveals incredible details of the Didymos system. Scientists call Didymos a "rubble pile" asteroid , meaning it's a loose body made up of boulders, dust, gravel and other bits of the solar system held together by the asteroid's own gravity. In the image, many of these irregular boulders and rocks can be seen strewn across Didymos and its moonlet. Hera will reach the system on Nov. 25, and ESA will release the first full images from the mission.

science.title: China launching 1st international astronaut to Tiangong space station today: Watch it live
science.description: null China will send an international astronaut to its Tiangong space station today (Nov. 24) for the first time ever, and you can watch the landmark liftoff live. A Long March 2F rocket is scheduled to launch the Shenzhou-24 mission from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China today at 7:18 p.m. EST (0018 GMT and 8:18 a.m. Beijing time on Nov. 25). You can watch the liftoff live here at Space.com, courtesy of China Central Television (CCTV). China rolls out the Long March 2F rocket for its Shenzhou-24 astronaut mission on Nov. 17, 2026. (Image credit: CCTV) Shenzhou-24 will be China's 18th crewed spaceflight to date and its 12th astronaut mission to Tiangong , a three-module station that the nation finished assembling in low Earth orbit in late 2022. Those numbers may sound rather prosaic. But today's flight will make history, marking the first time that China has ever launched a foreign national to space. That trailblazer is Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces who will be the first person from his country ever to reach orbit. (Adventurer Namira Salim is the first Pakistani ever to fly to the final frontier, doing so on a Virgin Galactic suborbital mission in October 2023 .) China and Pakistan began paving Ali's path to Tiangong in February 2025 , with the signing of a spaceflight cooperation agreement in Islamabad. Pakistan then selected two astronaut candidates, who traveled to China for training. We didn't learn which Pakistani astronaut was picked for Shenzhou-24 until Monday night (Nov. 23), when China announced the mission's crew. This is not out of the ordinary, by the way; China generally doesn't reveal the identity of Shenzhou astronauts until the day before launch. This is in keeping with the nation's broader spaceflight ethos, which prizes keeping things close to the vest. Ali is flying as a payload specialist. The other Shenzhou-24 astronauts are commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer ​Wu Yi. Tang also flew on the Shenzhou-12 and Shenzhou-17 missions, which launched in June 2021 and October 2023, respectively. He will be the first person to visit Tiangong three times, according to the state-run Xinhua news agency. Shenzhou-24 will be the first spaceflight for Wu. Tang and Wu are expected to live aboard Tiangong for six months, the usual Shenzhou rotation. But Ali will stay in orbit for just a week or so, coming back down to Earth with Zhang Zhiyuan and Lai Ka-ying of the Shenzhou-23 mission, which launched on May 24 . According to the South China Morning Post, the third Shenzhou-23 crewmate, Zhu Yangzhu, will stay behind when Ali leaves, living aboard Tiangong until Shenzhou-24 comes home. Zhu will therefore become the first Chinese astronaut ever to spend a year in orbit, a milestone that will allow China to prep for long-duration missions to the moon and other deep-space locales.

science.title: Russia launches Progress 97 cargo ship to the International Space Station (video)
science.description: null Russia's latest freighter is on its way to the International Space Station. The robotic Progress 97 cargo craft launched atop a Soyuz rocket from the Russia-run Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan today (Nov. 24) at 5:17 a.m. EST (1013 GMT; 3:17 p.m. Baikonur time), carrying several tons of supplies for the astronauts aboard the orbiting lab. If all goes to plan, Progress 97 will arrive at the International Space Station (ISS) on Thursday (Nov. 26), docking with its Poisk module. But the freighter won't stay at that particular locale for long. A Russian Soyuz rocket launches the uncrewed Progress 97 cargo ship to the International Space Station from Baikonur Cosmodrome, Kazakhstan on Nov. 24, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) The cosmonauts currently living on the ISS — Pyotr Dubrov, Anna Kikina and Sergey Teteryatnikov — will unload Progress 97 through Poisk. But the freighter will then hop over to a different port, according to journalist and space historian Anatoly Zak: the aft one of the PrK transfer tunnel, which leads to Russia's Zvezda service module. The PrK port is the best site for engine burns that boost the orbit of the ISS, a service that Progress freighters regularly provide. But Progress 97 cannot unload its cargo through that port because the PrK transfer tunnel has been sealed off, due to an ongoing air leak that was first documented in 2019. Progress-97 is therefore "the first cargo mission scheduled to unload its cargo and perform orbit corrections of the ISS at different docking ports," Zak wrote on the site he runs, RussianSpaceWeb.com. Progress 96 cargo spacecraft packed with science and supplies approaches the International Space Station for a docking on Sept. 19, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) The Progress 97 mission, which Russia calls Progress MS-36, was originally expected to launch this past August, according to Zak. But the liftoff was pushed back several times, most significantly by the collapse of the service platform at Baikonur's Site 31 in November 2025. It took Russia about three months to repair the platform, leading to a series of delays. Progress 97 will likely stay docked to the ISS for about six months, after which it will be loaded up with trash and sent home to burn up in Earth's atmosphere . Japan's HTV-X vehicle and Northrop Grumman's Cygnus spacecraft are similarly expendable. The only currently operational ISS cargo craft that's reusable is SpaceX's Dragon capsule, which makes parachute-aided ocean splashdowns at the end of its missions.

science.title: Severe eczema healed by novel immune-calming pill in clinical trial
science.description: Eczema causes itchy, inflamed rashes on the skin Evgeniia Gordeeva/Getty Images Over a third of people with moderate to severe eczema taking part in a clinical trial have seen their skin completely or almost completely clear up after taking an experimental pill for four months. The drug targets a part of the immune system that causes eczema when it gets stuck in overdrive, and it may be preferable to the current standard treatment, which has to be injected. “It definitely looks promising,” says Gayle Ross at the Royal Melbourne Hospital. Read more Chronic inflammation messes with your mind. Here’s how to calm it Eczema, or atopic dermatitis, is a chronic skin condition characterised by itchy, inflamed rashes and broken skin that can become infected. It is driven by an overactive immune pathway involving two signalling proteins called interleukin-4 and interleukin-13. Advertisement In 2017, the companies Sanofi and Regeneron received approval in the US for their jointly developed eczema drug dupilumab, which blocks interleukin-4 and interleukin-13 signalling. But, although the medication is effective , it has had limited uptake in the US because it must be injected under the skin and costs up to $59,000 per year for those without insurance coverage. Now, another company, Kymera Therapeutics, has developed an alternative treatment that can be taken in pill form, called KT-621. It targets the same immune pathway as dupilumab but degrades a protein called STAT6 that is activated downstream from interleukin-4 and interleukin-13 in the development of eczema. Free newsletter Sign up to Health Check Sign up to newsletter In the clinical trial , 244 adults with an average age of 39 and moderate to severe eczema were randomised to take KT-621 at three different doses or a placebo pill every day for 16 weeks. Those taking the most effective dose experienced an average 72 per cent reduction in their eczema severity on a standard scale, compared to 27 per cent in the placebo group. What’s more, 38 per cent of participants taking KT-621 had completely healed skin or almost completely healed skin by the end of the trial. “These results exceeded our expectations,” said Terence Rooney , the chief medical officer of Kymera Therapeutics, when announcing the results in a webcast on 23 November. He showed before-and-after photos of one man who had had severe eczema all over his torso at the beginning of the trial, which disappeared by the end. “It’s obviously early days and the trial had relatively small patient numbers, but [KT-621] looks like it has similar efficacy to dupilumab, which is currently the standard of care for moderate to severe atopic dermatitis, and it would be nice to have an oral option as opposed to an injection,” says Ross. science.title: November's full moon rises tonight! Here's how to see the Beaver Moon supermoon
science.description: null Get ready stargazers! The full "Beaver supermoon" rises in the eastern sky, offering up a spectacular display shortly after sunset tonight (Nov. 24). Here's what you need to know. November's full moon occurs at 9:53 a.m. EST (1453 GMT) on Nov. 24, as the lunar disk passes opposite the sun in our sky, making it appear fully lit from our perspective. The November full moon is often referred to as the Beaver Moon because it rises around the time the small mammals are hard at work building their lodges in preparation for the winter. Viewers in the U.S. can even get a detailed look at the full moon ahead of local moonrise thanks to a free supermoon livestream from the Virtual Telescope Project (VTP), starting at 10:30 a.m. EST (1530 GMT) today. The stream will feature live views of the lunar disk captured from the VTP's robotic telescopes in Manciano, Italy, weather permitting. The Beaver Moon is also set to be a dazzling supermoon , because it turns full as the natural satellite passes within 90% of perigee , when it is at its closest to Earth in its 27-day elliptical orbit. A supermoon's proximity can make it appear 30% brighter and 14% larger than the most distant full moon of the year, which is colloquially known as a "micro-moon". When to see the Beaver Moon November's full moon will be below the horizon for stargazers in the U.S. at the moment it turns full. Instead, viewers in America should look out for the moon shortly after sunset on Nov. 24, as it looms low over the eastern horizon. A supermoon can make for a spectacular sight when caught close to the horizon. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) Try covering the lunar disk with your thumb to block out the worst of its glare, and you may just be able to spot to blue-white lights of the Pleiades open star cluster glimmering less than 10 degrees away — roughly the width of your clenched fist held at arm's length. If you miss the full moon on Nov. 24, don't worry as the moon will appear full to the casual observer for a couple more nights, so there's no excuse to miss it! Remember to check out Time and Date's moonrise and moonset tracker for timings specific to your location. What should I expect from the November supermoon? You may see the moon turn a striking orange-yellow hue as it rises because sunlight reflected from its disk passes through more of Earth's atmosphere, which scatters shorter bluer wavelengths of light and allows more red and orange light to reach our eyes in a process called Rayleigh scattering. Check out our full Celestron Nexstar 4SE review for more. Signs of unrest began in late October 2026. On October 27, seismic sensors recorded a sharp uptick in activity, and Japan’s Meteorological Agency reported that the first photographs of the eruption were captured. Soon after, sensors on several satellites began to capture an array of observations. The OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 captured the left image on October 26, when the coast was still quiet. On November 11, Landsat 9 got its first clear view of the land the submarine volcano has built (right). A shortwave-infrared signature, a sign of the eruption’s heat, is shown in orange. A faint gray volcanic plume drifts southeast of the vent, and a streak of floating pumice stretches across the water in the same direction. A false-color backscatter radar image from the NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) satellite offered an even earlier look at the eruption. On October 28, despite heavy cloud cover, the radar detected a large disturbance in the water in the same area that erupted in December 2023. When the clouds cleared in early November, the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) and VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) sensors on NASA and NOAA satellites also captured signs of the ongoing eruption’s volcanic plumes and infrared signature . Japan’s Coast Guard released a report on November 16 confirming the formation of new land connected to the pre-existing beach. The eruption appears to have added roughly 50 hectares (125 acres) of new beach, about the area of 90 American football fields. That would enlarge the island by about 1.7 percent. The new land adjoins the southeast beach where American troops landed on February 19, 1945, beginning one of the bloodiest battles in the history of the U.S. Marines. The location of the eruption is no surprise to scientists. In addition to the 2023 eruption off the southeast coast, Iwo Jima had an eruption off its west coast in August 2025, said Daniel Slayback, a scientist at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center.
